target: Sun's disjoint-coset conjecture (Internat. J. Math. 17 (2006) Conjecture 1.2) at k = 6 for EVERY group: if a_1G_1, ..., a_6G_6 are pairwise disjoint left cosets of subgroups of finite index in a group G, then gcd([G:G_i],[G:G_j]) >= 6 for some i < j; or an exact counterexample.

exact_statement.groups: arbitrary groups G; subgroups of finite index, possibly equal; cosets pairwise disjoint (not a cover)
exact_statement.sharpness: 6 cosets of one subgroup of index 6

primary.source: Z.-W. Sun, Internat. J. Math. 17 (2006) 1047-1064, Conjecture 1.2 (arXiv math/0501451v4), read at k = 6
primary.book: 10000 Selected Problems, mathematics volume p. 106 (PDF p. 122), article by Sun Zhi-Wei: the general conjecture is "far from solved"

status_statements_known: Sun MathOverflow Q316709 (2018-12-02): k=5 confirmed by Zhu Gong in 2010 (unpublished); 'Since 2010, there is no further progress on the conjecture.'
Fornal-Sun arXiv 2607.24655 and PPL 057 (2026-07-27): k=3,4 proved for groups
For G = Z: k <= 20 (O'Bryant); Menon 2608.15873: transfer from Z to groups fails at length 5

Parent screen S/math-1-sun-coset5-post-candidate-priority-v1.md: Sun 2024 slides list k = 3,4 (Zhu) and k = 5 (Gong 2009, unpublished) only; no k >= 6 claim located in bounded scope (a search miss is not novelty).
reduction_parent_check: Parent re-derived R1(6) by hand at freeze. Every gcd is a prime power in {2,3,4,5}, so the 15 pairs are exactly covered by cliques A_p, p in {2,3,5}, with |A_p ∩ A_q| <= 1. Size multisets with every |A_p| <= 5 sum to 15 only as {4,4,3}, which needs 7 points. So some A_p has all six indices. p=3 is excluded by Zhu k=4. p=2 splits into Zhu k=3 / M-S Prop 4.5 / Core(5). p=5 is Core5(6). This is not yet a hostile review.
first_obligation: Parent runs the k=6-specific priority pre-check in parallel. The worker STOPS at once if told that a prior k=6 group claim (published or reported unpublished) exists.

Freeze the reduction R1(6): Sun(6) <=> Core5(6), given Zhu Thm 1.1, Prop 4.5 (sun-coset5 proof-v3 section 2) and Core(5) (sun-coset5 proof-v3). Write the written proof (k6-assessment-v1.md section 2) as a lane README lemma. Record the explicit dependence on Core(5) being verified.

Freeze rules-k6-v1 (T, K, P, F/H1, Lemma R, H2-analogue, any constant-alpha lemma), each with explicit hypotheses and a written proof, before any counted enumeration. Split E2 by v2(r) in {1, >=2}. Prove that E5 is irrelevant or carry it as a status.

Write a frozen, deterministic standard-library backtracking enumerator. It assigns alpha in {1,2,3,4} to the 15 edges of K6 for each special assignment (E2 class, E3), applies triangle tau-pruning, and gives canonical (S6) orbit reduction. It outputs one certificate per pattern orbit and the exact survivor list.
Write a second, independently coded checker over all labelled patterns, or over a provably complete canonical set, before any proof claim.
Attack the survivors with written lemmas. A counterexample candidate must be an explicit finite group with explicit cosets, verified by two independent exact checks plus a parent recomputation.
controls: The same engine, with constants changed, reproduces Core_3(4) (M-S Prop 4.3 / Zhu k=4) and Core(5) (sun-coset5 engine-v1 orbit counts and its single S-D survivor).

Realisable configurations survive every rule on exact data: five cosets of an index-5 subgroup; explicit A5 families with indices 5r; random realisable families in small permutation groups (sanity only, never evidence).
Selected intended-reason mutation demonstrations for every certificate type.
Controls record observations only; none gates the run.
partial_result_definition: A PARTIAL result consists of: (a) the frozen written reduction Sun(6) <=> Core5(6); (b) frozen rules with written proofs; (c) a frozen enumeration giving one certificate per killed pattern orbit and the exact survivor list (alpha matrix, E2 class, E3); (d) any survivor eliminated by a written lemma, recorded separately. A partial result is NOT the gate. Small-group or permutation-group searches are never gate evidence.
acceptance: GATE: a complete written proof of Core5(6), computer-assisted certificates allowed if independently replayed, covering every pattern orbit; OR an exact counterexample verified by two independent exact checkers plus a parent recomputation. Both also require: parent re-derivation of R1(6) and of every rule used; parent-independent replay of all certificates; hostile reviews from both CLI families (Codex gpt-6.1-sol and Claude claude-opus-5-5); a post-result priority audit. The gate is conditional on the Core(5) result (sun-coset5 proof-v3) passing its own verification. Wording must state that dependence.
dependence: The gate is conditional on the Core(5) result (sun-coset5 proof-v3 and the parent bridge PASS) receiving its own parent correctness verdict. Branch p=2 inherits that status. k=5 itself carries a prior unpublished claim (Gong), which does not affect the openness of k=6.
resources: At most 2 concurrent processes and at most 4 GiB RSS within the math-1 lane caps; compiled helpers allowed if source-hashed before use; standard library; kilobyte-to-megabyte outputs; files created exclusively; corrections in new versions; TMPDIR inside the lane; no solver farms; never SIGKILL.
stop_rules: Stop on any prior claim of k=6 for groups, published or reported unpublished.
Small-group or permutation-group searches are never gate evidence.
If the frozen enumeration plus rules leaves survivors and none is eliminated by 15:30 PDT, report PARTIAL with the exact survivor list.
A claimed counterexample needs two independent exact checks plus a parent recomputation.
New science stops at 17:30 PDT 2026-10-18; native work ends 17:57.
If the parent's Core(5) verification fails, stop and report: R1(6) branch p=2 is then unsupported.
